description: This bar chart, from the paper "MIG Automatic Data Selection for Instruction Tuning by Maximizing Information Gain in Semantic Space," illustrates quality scores for two methods, IFD and DEITA, across four distinct metrics: Base Avg<sub>all</sub>, Base Avg<sub>sub</sub>, Avg<sub>all</sub>, and Avg<sub>sub</sub>. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by method (IFD and DEITA), while the vertical axis represents "Scores" on a linear scale ranging from 30 to 70. A legend in the upper right identifies the four metrics by color: Base Avg<sub>all</sub> is represented by a blue dashed line, Base Avg<sub>sub</sub> by a yellow dashed line, Avg<sub>all</sub> by a light blue bar, and Avg<sub>sub</sub> by a salmon-colored bar. For each method, two bars are displayed: the light blue bar (Avg<sub>all</sub>) is consistently taller than the salmon bar (Avg<sub>sub</sub>). Specifically, for IFD, the Avg<sub>all</sub> score is 63.98 and the Avg<sub>sub</sub> score is 41.90; for DEITA, the Avg<sub>all</sub> score is 67.64 and the Avg<sub>sub</sub> score is 42.99. The chart also includes two horizontal reference lines: a blue dashed line at 63.98 (corresponding to the IFD Avg<sub>all</sub> score) and a yellow dashed line at 39.13 (corresponding to the IFD Avg<sub>sub</sub> score), which appear to be the average scores for the respective metrics across the two methods. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and labeling.
